intro: Yasothon is a small town, and most of its lodging is plain block hotels or simple guesthouses · U-Sabai Villa stands out the moment you arrive — a clean white two-storey minimalist villa with just 8 rooms, tucked into Soi Chaeng Sanit 1 within the town municipality · Opened in 2024, the rooms still feel brand new · The draw here is quiet, cleanliness, and owner-run hospitality that includes free breakfast and unlimited afternoon snacks · Scored 9.7 from 34 Trip.com reviews, from approx. ฿850/night

body.html: U-Sabai Villa is a two-storey property that only opened in 2024 · The whole building holds just 8 rooms, which makes the atmosphere noticeably different from the usual in-town Yasothon hotel — no big lobby, no crowds, just a small garden, a patio in front of each room, and a shared lounge the owner set up for sipping coffee · Several reviewers describe it as "like staying with relatives" rather than checking into a hotel.

Rooms are minimalist, in white and pale-wood tones, around 21–22 sqm · There are VIP single beds, large 6-foot doubles, and twin rooms with two beds · Every room has air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, free bottled water, and an en-suite bathroom with a hot shower and free toiletries · Some rooms have a private patio or terrace facing the garden · Because it's a new build, everything still feels fresh and works well — and cleanliness is the single thing guests praise most.
"Brand-new, spotlessly clean, so quiet I slept beautifully. Woke up to breakfast laid out, and in the afternoon they brought snacks too — it really felt like being looked after."

What pushes the score so high is the free food · Breakfast is a freshly cooked Isan/Thai home-style spread served in the morning, and there's a round of afternoon snacks on top of it · Many guests note the portions are more generous than you'd expect at this price · The owner and staff are attentive, reply to messages fast, and recommend places to eat and visit around town — the kind of host-led service you rarely get at a large block hotel.

The location is on Soi Chaeng Sanit 1, across from Krua Rachawadee restaurant · It sits inside Mueang Yasothon municipality, a few minutes' drive from the Ban Singha Tha old town, the evening market, and Wiman Phaya Thaen park · It suits self-drivers best thanks to free parking and a quiet soi · Without a car you may need to rely on a motorbike taxi or a rental, since the villa isn't on a main road or near the bus terminal.

Honestly, U-Sabai Villa isn't a full-facility hotel · There's no pool, no gym, no lift, and only 8 rooms in total · If you're after a resort with on-site activities or a big hotel with an all-day restaurant, this won't be the right fit · But if what you want is a fresh, clean, quiet room at an easy price with a warm homestay feel — it delivers exactly that, on purpose.

With so few rooms and consistently high review scores, U-Sabai Villa fills up fast during festivals, especially Yasothon's Bun Bang Fai (Rocket Festival) in May when crowds pour into town · If you're planning around then, book several weeks ahead · The rest of the year, 1–2 weeks' notice is usually enough, and you'll often get a better rate than walking in.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — U-Sabai Villa Yasothon

faq.q: Where is U-Sabai Villa in Yasothon, and is it easy to reach?
faq.a: U-Sabai Villa is at 28 Soi Chaeng Sanit 1, Nai Mueang, Mueang Yasothon, across from Krua Rachawadee restaurant · It sits within the town municipality, a few minutes' drive from the Ban Singha Tha old town and fresh market · It's easiest if you're self-driving, thanks to free parking; without a car you may need a motorbike taxi.

faq.q: What's the starting price at U-Sabai Villa, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿850/night for a VIP single · There are double rooms, a large 6-foot bed room, and a twin room, all around 21–22 sqm, climbing to roughly ฿1,100 · Rates vary by date, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is U-Sabai Villa best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples, solo travellers, and small families driving to Yasothon · The focus is on quiet, cleanliness, and a homestay feel · It's not for travellers who want a pool, gym, or the facilities of a large hotel.

Yes — a free home-style breakfast cooked fresh is served in the morning, with a round of afternoon snacks on top · Many reviewers say the portions are generous and great value for a property at this price.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book U-Sabai Villa?
faq.a: Because there are only 8 rooms and review scores are high, it fills fast — especially around Yasothon's Bun Bang Fai (Rocket Festival) in May, when you should book several weeks ahead · The rest of the year, 1–2 weeks' notice is usually enough and often gets a better rate than walking in.
